Your data & privacy

VeraFuel records the food, training, sleep and body data you choose to log, so the app can calculate your targets and show your progress.

What we store: your entries are saved to your own device and securely synced so you don't lose them. Nothing is shared with other users.

During this beta: the VeraFuel team may review anonymised, aggregated data to fix bugs and improve the app — including new foods you add, which may be added to the shared food library to benefit everyone.

Your control: the data is yours. You can ask us to delete it at any time, and you can stop using the app whenever you like.

This is health-related information, and we treat it with care and in line with data-protection law.

I understand how my data is used and I agree to take part in the VeraFuel beta.

Your personalised loading plan
Race day morning
During the race & recovery
Best plant-based carb sources for loading
Science note: Glycogen storage peaks at 10-12g carbohydrate/kg/day for 36-48h prior to event (Burke et al., 2011). Choose low-fibre carb sources during loading to minimise GI distress. Avoid high-fat and high-fibre foods 48h before event.

Protein intelligence
Leucine threshold: Each meal needs ~2.5g leucine to maximally stimulate muscle protein synthesis (MPS). Plant sources require larger portions to hit this threshold.

Creatine status
Not tracked
Log your daily creatine intake to track muscle saturation.
Muscle saturation 0%
Plant-based athletes have ~20-30% lower baseline muscle creatine than omnivores — meaning you get a proportionally larger performance response from supplementation.
Log creatine today
0g logged
Loading phase: 5g × 4/day for 5-7 days (fastest saturation)
Maintenance: 3-5g/day (keep muscles saturated)
Best time: Post-workout with carbs for best uptake
Iron absorption optimiser Bioavailability
Log meals to see iron bioavailability analysis
Estimated absorption is a directional guide to help you pair foods well — not a clinical measurement, and not for diagnosing or managing iron deficiency. If you’re concerned about iron status, ask your GP for a blood test.

Non-haem iron (plant sources) absorbs at 2-20% depending on meal composition. Vitamin C increases absorption up to 3×. Tea, coffee and calcium within 1hr reduce it.

Recovery factors today
Recovery toolkit
🧂 Your sweat & salt profile
We're all built differently — some lose far more sodium than others. Answer these and VeraFuel personalises your hydration and salt targets. No lab test needed.
💧 Sweat rate calculator
Weigh yourself (dry) before and after a session, note what you drank, and get your personal fluid plan. The standard sports-science field method.
☕ Caffeine for performance
One of the best-evidenced legal boosts — but the right dose is personal. Set yours and VeraFuel gives you a pre-session plan tuned to your bodyweight and sensitivity.

The true picture
Weight alone hides what's changing. Fat mass and lean mass show what you're actually losing or building. Tap to show or hide each line.
Fat & lean mass are derived from weight × body-fat readings. Smart-scale numbers are rough in absolute terms — trust the direction of the lines, not any single day.

Evidence-based targets
Your carb and calorie goals scale with each day's training intensity, following published sports nutrition guidelines.
Your coach assessment
How we set your targets

Your body's fuel needs aren't fixed — they rise and fall with how hard you train. A rest day and a hard interval session call for very different amounts of carbohydrate.

So instead of one flat number, VeraFuel scales your daily carbs and calories to the intensity you tag for each day:

Rest
lower carbs, supports recovery and repair without excess fuel
Easy
moderate fuelling for low-intensity sessions and active recovery
Hard
higher carbs to power quality training and maximise adaptation
Endurance
high carbs for long, sustained efforts where glycogen is the limiting factor
Race
peak fuelling and carb loading for event day performance

This "fuel for the work required" approach is the consensus of leading sports nutrition bodies, which recommend carbohydrate intake ranging from roughly 3 to 12 g per kg of body weight per day depending on training load.

Thomas DT, Erdman KA, Burke LM. Nutrition and Athletic Performance — Joint Position Stand. J Acad Nutr Diet. 2016;116(3):501–528.

Burke LM et al. Carbohydrates for training and competition. J Sports Sci. 2011;29(sup1):S17–S27.

Impey SG et al. Fuel for the Work Required: A Theoretical Framework for CHO Periodisation. Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab. 2018;28(5):353–363.

Areta JL et al. Timing and distribution of protein ingestion during recovery from resistance exercise. J Physiol. 2013;591(9):2319–2331.

Norton LE & Layman DK. Leucine regulates translation initiation of protein synthesis in skeletal muscle. J Nutr. 2006;136(2):533S–537S.

Kreider RB et al. ISSN position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:18.

Hallberg L & Hulthen L. Prediction of dietary iron absorption. Am J Clin Nutr. 2000;71(5):1147–1160.

van Vliet S et al. The skeletal muscle anabolic response to plant- versus animal-based protein consumption. J Nutr. 2015;145(9):1981–1991.

Morton RW et al. Meta-analysis of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength. Br J Sports Med. 2018;52(6):376–384.

Smith GI et al. Dietary omega-3 fatty acid supplementation increases muscle protein synthesis. Am J Clin Nutr. 2011;93(2):402–412.

Hirshkowitz M et al. National Sleep Foundation sleep time duration recommendations. Sleep Health. 2015;1(1):40–43.

VeraFuel provides general guidance based on published sports nutrition research. It is not a substitute for personalised advice — for a plan tailored to you, consult a registered dietitian or sports nutritionist.
